title: Substrings of Size Three with Distinct Characters
prompt: A string is called a good string if there are no repeated characters. Given a string `s`, return the number of good substrings of length 3 in `s`. Note that if there are multiple occurrences of the same substring, every occurrence should be counted.

examples.explanation: The substrings of length 3 are "xyz", "yzz", "zza", and "zaz". Only "xyz" has 3 distinct characters.
The good substrings are "abc", "bca", "cab", and "abc" again.
The string is shorter than 3 characters, so there are no length-3 substrings at all

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only
hints: This is a fixed-size window of length 3 slid across the string.
For each window, you just need to know whether all three characters are distinct.
Instead of re-checking uniqueness from scratch for every window, you can check it directly with a small set (only 3 elements) for each of the n-2 windows in O(n) total.

solution.approach: Slide a fixed window of size 3 across the string. For each window position, check whether the 3 characters it contains are all distinct by comparing set size to 3. Since the window is always exactly 3 characters, this check is O(1), giving an overall O(n) scan.
